name: Ehrwalder Alm
kurzbeschreibung: The Ehrwalder Alm at 1,500 m at the foot of the Zugspitze: modern 8-seater gondola, barrier-free Tirolerhaus, and the gateway to Seebensee and Drachensee.
preis: Berg- und Talfahrt Erwachsene 26,00 €, Kinder (6–15 J.) 16,00 €
oeffnungszeiten: Mitte Mai bis Anfang Nov täglich 08:30–16:30 Uhr (Hochsommer ab 08:00–17:30 Uhr)
beschreibung:
Overview

The Ehrwalder Alm spreads out as a spacious, sunny high plateau at approximately 1,500 metres above sea level at the southwestern foot of the mighty Wettersteingebirge in Ehrwald. Nestled between the rock massifs of the Zugspitze (2,962 m) and the Mieminger Kette, this high valley is one of the most popular excursion destinations in the Tiroler Zugspitz Arena. Whether it is a leisurely family walk around the Almsee, relaxation on sunny panoramic sun terraces, or an ambitious mountain hike to the crystal-clear alpine lakes Seebensee and Drachensee – the Ehrwalder Alm offers unforgettable nature experiences for every generation.

History & Mountain Cable Car

Touristic development began in 1962 with the construction of the first chairlift. In 2001, the system was completely modernized and replaced by the high-performance 8-seater monocable gondola lift Ehrwalder Almbahn, which whisks guests from the valley station (1,108 m) to the top station at 1,502 metres in just around eight minutes. At the end of 2022, the lift company upgraded the cable car with 99 state-of-the-art, barrier-free panoramic cabins manufactured by Carvatech. Directly at the mountain station, the multi-award-winning flagship mountain restaurant Tirolerhaus opened in 2012, combining traditional alpine cosiness with contemporary timber architecture. From the pasture, the classic hike leads to Seebenalm and onwards to the emerald-green Seebensee (1,657 m), whose mirror-like waters picturesquely reflect the rock faces of the Zugspitze. Even higher up, the Coburger Hütte (1,920 m) overlooks the mysterious Drachensee.

Visit & Getting There

The summer season of the Ehrwalder Almbahn typically runs from mid-May to early November, daily from 08:30 to 16:30 (during peak summer from July to September starting earlier from 08:00 to 17:30). In winter, the ski season lasts from mid-December until Easter. Cable car tickets for summer 2025/2026: ascent and descent for adults €26.00 (single trip €17.00), youth (ages 16–18) €21.00, children (ages 6–15) €16.00, children under 6 ride free; family tickets from €59.50. Getting there by public transport: take the Außerfernbahn railway (ÖBB/DB) to Ehrwald station, where the regional hiking and guest bus (Line 1) runs directly to the Ehrwald Almbahn stop. By car: toll-free from the north via Garmisch-Partenkirchen to Ehrwald or from the south over the Fernpass (B179); large free parking lots are available directly at the valley station (Kroppbühel 10).

Tips

The Ehrwalder Almbahn and the Tirolerhaus mountain restaurant feature exemplary barrier-free facilities: the gondolas stop without steps for wheelchair users and strollers, and the restaurant offers certified accessible restrooms. The circular trail around the Ehrwalder Almsee directly at the top station is suitable for prams; free handcarts (Bollerwagen) can also be borrowed at the mountain station. (Note: the alpine trail up to Coburger Hütte is not suitable for strollers). On hot midsummer days, catch the first gondola at 08:00 to hike to Seebensee.
